subject: Customer escalation: TTFT p95/p99 regressions linked to upstream TLS renegotiation — exec attention
messages:
From: Andrew Li <andrew.li@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: brightcart-status@pagerduty.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in TTFT / p99 — customer facing latency, urgent

Marissa —

We're seeing a material regression in Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) from the Redwood Hosted API for our production traffic in us-west-2 starting ~08:20 PDT today. p95 jumped from ~180ms to 900-1,200ms and p99s are spiking above 2s. This is impacting checkout flows and causing timeouts in our synchronous paths.

Attached is a ZIP with sample request/response traces and a screenshot from our synthetic monitor. Key observations from our side:
- Errors: elevated TLS handshake failures (ECONNRESET/TLS handshake failed) reported in client-side logs around the same time window
- Throughput: overall request rate steady, but successful responses fall ~8% in short bursts
- Region: primarily impacting us-west-2 (we see some blips in us-east but much smaller)

Can you confirm whether there are any CDN or upstream network issues on your side? We need an ETA for a mitigation; business impact is high.

Attachments: brightcart-ttft-logs-20260825.zip, screenshot-ttft-dashboard.png

Thanks,
Andrew
Director, Site Reliability — BrightCart

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Li <andrew.li@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in TTFT / p99 — customer facing latency, urgent

Thanks for the heads up Andrew — we're on it. I've looped in our Infrastructure and Networking leads (Karthik, Aditya).

Immediate asks:
- Karthik/Aditya: can you prioritize triage on CDN edges -> upstream NLB TLS renegotiation symptoms? The customer logs indicate handshake resets coincident with TTFT spikes.
- Andrew: any specific request IDs you want us to prioritize? The attached traces are helpful — we'll correlate with internal telemetry.

I'll keep BrightCart and their CSM updated. If this looks like a region-wide regression we may need to engage Exec Ops for routing fallbacks.

— Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in TTFT / p99 — initial triage notes

Marissa / Aditya —

Quick triage update (summary of first-pass analysis against internal traces):
- Scope: Elevated TTFT/p95/p99 primarily from requests routed through CDN POPs in us-west. Synthetic probes corroborate customer timing regressions beginning ~08:18 PDT.
- Observed symptom: repeated TLS renegotiation and occasional handshake timeouts between CDN edge and our regional NLB. Packet captures show extra round trips (~+1 RTT) during affected flows which maps to the increased TTFT.
- Error pattern: higher TLS alerts (internal: "handshake_failure" followed by connection reset). No sustained increase in server CPU or GPU time.
- Correlation: a recent CDN configuration push (certificate rotation + keepalive policy tweak) rolled out earlier today in us-west POPs per CDN partner release notes. We're requesting historical release metadata.

Immediate mitigations we can run in parallel:
1) Temporarily extend TLS session keepalive/timeout on the NLB side to reduce renegotiation frequency (low risk).
2) Add a short-edge circuit-breaker: if an edge reports >5% handshake failures for 5m, route that edge's traffic to alternate POPs.
3) If needed, move BrightCart's primary routing to an adjacent region (us-east-1) for a short period (requires ops coordination).

Next steps:
- Aditya to check whether we can flip keepalive on the NLB immediately (hotfix).
- I'll request the CDN partner to roll back the keepalive change for us-west POPs and push packet capture windows for deeper debugging.

I'll post findings as soon as I have the partner response.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in TTFT / p99 — NLB keepalive hotfix planned

Team —

I can push a short-lived NLB keepalive extension and enable more aggressive session caching to reduce full TLS handshakes. Estimated rollout: 12 minutes for config + 5 minutes to observe. Risk: minimal; config is per-region and reversible.

I'll also stand up packet capture for the next 30 minutes on the affected NLB and forward PCAPs to Karthik and the CDN partner. If we still see >3% handshake failures after the keepalive change, we should plan an edge-routing fallback for BrightCart.

I'll proceed unless you object.

-Aditya
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Li <andrew.li@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in TTFT / p99 — immediate mitigations in progress

Andrew —

Thanks for the traces. Our initial mitigation (NLB keepalive extension + session cache warm) was rolled in us-west-2 at 10:23 PDT. Early telemetry shows p95 reduced from ~1.0s down to ~320-350ms within 10 minutes and p99 improved from ~2.1s to ~750ms. TLS handshake error rate dropped by ~70% in the affected POPs.

We're continuing to monitor and working with the CDN partner to revert the configuration that appears to have triggered extra renegotiations at edge POPs.

Next actions:
- We'll provide a root-cause update once CDN partner confirms rollout history and we analyze PCAPs.
- I'll share a short exec summary for BrightCart's leadership with the remediation timeline and follow-up plan.

I'll keep you updated hourly for the next 3 hours. Please flag if you see any regression.

Regards,
Marissa

From: Andrew Li <andrew.li@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: brightcart-status@pagerduty.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in TTFT / p99 — thanks + request for timeline

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the quick response and the mitigation. We're seeing much better numbers on synthetic monitors and a dramatic drop in production errors. Can you confirm the expected timeline for:
1) Complete rollback of the CDN keepalive/config change in us-west POPs (partner ETA)
2) Postmortem and permanent mitigation (e.g., hardened keepalive defaults, expanded session caching) — expected date and owners

We need the postmortem for our internal incident report and to present to stakeholders tomorrow.

Appreciate the fast work here.

-Andrew
Director, Site Reliability — BrightCart
